questions.question: What OS analogy does MemGPT build on?
options: Processes and threads, where each memory tool call spawns a new OS-level thread
Virtual memory: main context as RAM, external store as disk, memory tools as page in and out
Network sockets, where the agent opens a persistent connection to its memory store
File descriptors, where every memory read consumes a slot until it is closed
questions.explanation: MemGPT maps prompt to RAM, external store to disk, and memory tools to page-fault-style transfers.

questions.question: Why do bigger context windows not fully solve memory?
options: Because most providers cap the effective window at 4k tokens regardless of the sticker limit
Because sending a longer context costs nothing extra in latency or dollars to the caller
Overflow, dilution of attention, and lack of cross-session persistence still bite even with 128k windows
Because the model refuses to process any input longer than a few thousand tokens
questions.explanation: Mem0 measured 128k-window baselines still missing facts a 4k agent with external memory catches; overflow, dilution, and persistence remain.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of MemGPT's canonical memory tools?
options: core_memory_append, which writes to a persistent section of the prompt
archival_memory_search, which retrieves results from the searchable external store
conversation_search, which scans past turns for a matching fact
gradient_memory_update, which backpropagates a memory update into the weights
questions.explanation: There is no gradient memory tool; the surface is core/archival/conversation operations.

questions.question: What does the interrupt pattern do in MemGPT?
options: Mid-conversation the agent invokes a memory tool and the result splices into the next turn as an observation
It halts the entire agent run the moment any tool call anywhere raises an error at all
It bypasses the context window entirely and writes straight into the model's weights
It triggers a full retrain of the underlying model on the current conversation transcript
questions.explanation: Memory-as-interrupt: invoke memory tool, runtime fetches, result returns as a new observation on the next turn (like a Unix read()).

questions.question: Which production system did MemGPT evolve into in 2024?
options: Mem0, a hybrid memory library built independently on top of the same pattern
Letta, the company MemGPT's own team formed to productionize the design
Zep, a third-party memory service aimed at a similar problem space
Pinecone, a managed vector database product used by many memory systems
questions.explanation: MemGPT became Letta in September 2024; the research repo cpacker/MemGPT still exists as the origin.

questions.question: What is memory poisoning in this context?
options: A bug in the vector index that silently corrupts nearest-neighbor lookups on every single query
Reading from the disk-tier store even when the RAM-tier context still has plenty of room
An attacker's content gets stored as a memory note and is re-ingested on future recalls
Drift between the embedding model version used to write a note and the one used to read it back
questions.explanation: External memory is retrieved text; if attacker-reachable content lands in a memory note the agent re-ingests it next session.
